# Apply Fixes

## Change Summary

No further fixes were applied in this stage. The third review approved the implemented amendments as-is, so the codebase remained unchanged and this pass only records that the remaining notes were non-blocking follow-ups outside the scope of this bead.

## Steps

0. [Completed] Reviewed the approved validation output from completion round 3 to determine whether any actionable fixes remained after the latest remediation pass.
1. [Completed] Confirmed that the remaining review notes were non-blocking follow-ups only and did not require additional source, test, documentation, or backlog changes for this bead.
2. [Skipped] Apply further code or documentation fixes.
3. [Completed] Recorded the approved outcome and carried forward the existing validation record because no code changed in this pass.

## Validation Evidence

- `run-20260327155320-review-c1-a1-cr3` concluded with `outcome: approved`.
- No new code changes were made in this pass, so no additional validation commands were necessary.
- The current validation record remains the previously successful runs: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test -q -p tank_core --test cycling`, `cargo test -q -p tank_scenarios --test startup_overrides`, `cargo test --quiet`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` (with only the pre-existing unrelated `derivable_impls` warning).

## Outstanding Risks

- A pre-existing `clippy::derivable_impls` warning in `tank_scenarios::StartupOverrides` remains for a separate housekeeping pass.
- Decomposer DOC and DO half-saturation parameters still use total-mass units; the broader concentration-based kinetic normalization is intentionally deferred to downstream beads `tanksim-6e5.2.3`, `tanksim-6e5.2.4`, and `tanksim-6e5.2.5`.
- Startup override rebuilding now correctly restores source-water chemistry after substrate changes during initial materialization, but any future flow that needs to preserve intentionally aged chemistry across substrate swaps will require an explicit alternate mode.
